application_questions.question: A square lawn in a Melbourne park has side length $x\text{ m}$. One pair of opposite sides is increased by $5\text{ m}$ and the other pair is decreased by $2\text{ m}$ to form a rectangle. Write an expanded quadratic expression for the area of the rectangle.

A square swimming pool of side length $x\text{ m}$ is surrounded by a uniform paved path of width $2\text{ m}$ on all four sides. Expand $(x + 4)^2 - x^2$ to find a simplified expression for the area of the path, and evaluate it when $x = 10$.
Use the difference of two squares identity $(a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2$ to mentally evaluate $47 \times 53$ by writing it as $(50 - 3)(50 + 3)$.
A rectangular solar panel has length $(3x + 2)\text{ cm}$ and width $(2x - 1)\text{ cm}$. Find an expanded expression for its area and calculate the area when $x = 10$.

reasoning_questions.question: Sam expands $(x + 5)^2$ as $x^2 + 25$. Use an area diagram of a square of side $(x + 5)$ split into four regions to explain what missing terms Sam forgot.
reasoning_questions.answer: Splitting the side into $x$ and $5$ produces four regions of areas $x^2$, $5x$, $5x$, and $25$. Sam missed the two rectangular cross-terms $5x + 5x = 10x$, so $(x + 5)^2 = x^2 + 10x + 25$.

reasoning_questions.question: Prove algebraically that for any integer $n$, the product of one less than $n$ and one more than $n$, plus $1$, is always a perfect square.
reasoning_questions.answer: $(n - 1)(n + 1) + 1 = (n^2 - 1) + 1 = n^2$, which is the square of the integer $n$.

application_questions.question: Use the difference of two squares factorisation $a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)$ to evaluate $74^2 - 26^2$ without a calculator.
A circular washer has outer radius $R = 6.8\text{ cm}$ and inner hole radius $r = 3.2\text{ cm}$. Factorise the area formula $A = \pi R^2 - \pi r^2$ and hence find the exact area in terms of $\pi$.

A rectangular sheet of metal has area $(xy + 5x + 3y + 15)\text{ cm}^2$. Factorise by grouping to find the dimensions of the sheet in terms of $x$ and $y$.

reasoning_questions.question: Explain why $x^2 + 16$ cannot be factorised into linear factors over the real numbers, whereas $x^2 - 16$ factorises into $(x - 4)(x + 4)$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Expanding $(x + 4)^2$ gives $x^2 + 8x + 16$ and $(x - 4)^2$ gives $x^2 - 8x + 16$; only opposite signs $(x - 4)(x + 4)$ cancel the middle $x$-term, which makes the constant term $-16$, not $+16$. Also $x^2 + 16 \ge 16 > 0$ has no real roots.

reasoning_questions.question: When factorising $ab - 4a - 3b + 12$ by grouping the last two terms, why must we write $a(b - 4) - 3(b - 4)$ rather than $a(b - 4) - 3(b + 4)$?
reasoning_questions.answer: Factoring out $-3$ from $-3b + 12$ reverses the sign of $+12$ because $-3 \times (-4) = +12$, giving the matching binomial factor $(b - 4)$.

application_questions.answer: $(x + 7)\text{ m}$ by $(x + 5)\text{ m}$; when $x = 10$, $17\text{ m}$ by $15\text{ m}$

reasoning_questions.question: When factorising $x^2 + bx + c$ into $(x + p)(x + q)$, explain what the signs of $b$ and $c$ tell you about the signs of the integers $p$ and $q$ when (a) $c > 0$ and $b < 0$, and (b) $c < 0$.
reasoning_questions.answer: (a) Since $pq = c > 0$, $p$ and $q$ have the same sign, and since $p + q = b < 0$, both $p$ and $q$ are negative. (b) Since $pq = c < 0$, $p$ and $q$ have opposite signs (one positive, one negative).

reasoning_questions.question: Find all possible integer values of $b$ such that $x^2 + bx + 12$ can be factorised into $(x + p)(x + q)$ with integer values of $p$ and $q$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Factor pairs of $12$ are $(\pm 1, \pm 12), (\pm 2, \pm 6), (\pm 3, \pm 4)$, giving $b = p + q \in \{\pm 13, \pm 8, \pm 7\}$.
